newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak govt to tie wage growth to labour output.
newsitem.headline: Slovak govt to tie wage growth to labour output.

text.p: implement wage regulations to ensure salaries rise in accordance with industrial productivity increases, a senior finance ministry official said on Tuesday.

"The government is aware of the fact that wages have been growing far faster than labour productivity, and that is not healthy for the economy," Deputy Finance Minister Peter Stanek told journalists during a weekly government meeting.
"That is why the government will propose to the parliament some regulation of wage increases," Stanek said, adding the new measure should take effect from August 1, 1997.

He added the wage regulations should be aimed mainly at loss-making companies, where the government saw "inappropriately" high wages. Stanek did not comment further on the plan, saying more detailed information should be available after next week's government session.

The average real wage rose by 8.1 percent to total 8.198 crowns in the first quarter of this year, some 2.9 percentage points faster than labour productivity, the Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said earlier this month.
The average nominal wage for the period rose 14.6 percent, year-on-year.
Fast rising wages without the corresponding increase in productivity has been one of the biggest concerns voiced by analysts over the economy.
